IMPLEMENTATION REVIEW: APPROVED. Artifact located from tags: branch:worktree-knots-0b4c-lease-owner, commit:8a0e61cbc155 (pushed to origin). Reviewed the full origin/main...HEAD diff (20 files, +945/-23) against the acceptance criteria only.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, ONE BY ONE
1. 'LeaseData has an optional owner identity (machine id + pid) set on creation and round-tripping through event write -> push -> pull -> knot_hot': MET. LeaseOwner{machine_id,pid} on LeaseData (src/domain/lease.rs), stamped in create_lease (src/lease.rs). Round trip is proven end to end by replication::tests::lease_owner::pulled_foreign_lease_survives_sync_and_does_not_block_it, which authors a real knot.lease_data_set event on dev1, pushes to a bare origin, clones dev2, pulls, and reads owner machine_id/pid back out of dev2's knot_hot.
2. 'A lease created on machine A and pulled by machine B is not counted by the local active-lease query on B': MET. Same test asserts count_active_leases == 1 while count_local_active_leases == 0 for the pulling machine, then asserts push, pull, sync and sync_or_defer all succeed.
3. 'A lease whose owner is absent (legacy event) is counted as local': MET at three levels -- serde (lease_without_owner_is_treated_as_local), SQL (db::tests_lease_owner::lease_without_an_owner_counts_as_local, both machine ids see it), and behavior (the pre-existing push_blocks_with_active_leases still passes unchanged, since it inserts a LeaseData::default with no owner).
4. 'kno lease list and kno show surface the owning machine': MET. kno show emits a lease_owner field; kno lease list renders '(machine=<8 hex> pid=<n> this machine|another machine)'. Verified by hand on a scratch repo, not just by unit test.
5. 'require_no_active_leases and sync_or_defer_with_progress consult the owner-aware query': MET. Both now call ReplicationService::count_local_active_leases. KNOTS_ALLOW_ACTIVE_LEASE_REPLICATION escape hatch is untouched.
6. 'Machine id is stable across processes and adds no user identity': MET. Salted sha256 truncated to 32 hex, persisted at .knots/machine-id on first use; no hostname, username, or raw system id is stored (derived_machine_id_is_not_the_raw_system_id asserts the digest differs from its seed). .knots/machine-id is outside the index/events/snapshots stage set, so it never syncs.

OUT-OF-SCOPE GUARDS HELD: the sync guard still exists, no per-knot pull filtering was added, knots-ec23 and knots-0f9c scope untouched. No invariants on this knot.

SQL SAFETY: LOCAL_LEASE_PREDICATE is a compile-time constant and the machine id is a bound parameter, so no injection surface. json_extract is safe here because lease_data_json is NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}' and json1 is compiled in (-DSQLITE_ENABLE_JSON1).

DEVIATIONS FROM PLAN, ACCEPTED
a. Only one list helper shipped (lease::list_local_active_leases); the db-level list variant was dropped because it had no production consumer and would have been dead code under clippy -D warnings. Accepted: the knot's intent (an owner-aware local-lease query) is satisfied, and knots-0f9c can add a db-level list when it has a caller.
b. kno lease list default now shows only locally held active leases, printing 'no active leases held by this machine' when empty; --all still lists every lease with owner labels. This overrides my own plan-review directive. Accepted on review: the default listing answers 'what is blocking me here', and no visibility is lost because --all is labelled.
c. The replication sync test lives in src/replication/tests_lease_owner.rs, declared as a nested module inside src/replication/tests.rs. Verification step 3 named tests.rs; the 499-line repo cap made an in-file test impossible (tests.rs was already 459 lines). The test is in the replication::tests module tree and reuses its helpers, so the intent is met.
d. kno doctor stuck_leases deliberately still uses the owner-blind count_active_leases, so it can warn about a foreign lease that kno lease list no longer shows. Follow-up for knots-ec23 / knots-0f9c, not a blocker: it is a warn-level probe and doctor was explicitly out of this knot's scope.

GATES ACTUALLY RUN: make sanity green (cargo fmt --check, clippy --all-targets --all-features -D warnings, npm run check-changesets validating .changeset/lease-owner-machine-id.md, check-file-sizes.sh all files < 499, cargo test --all-targets --all-features with 1275 unit tests plus the integration suites, npm run test-release, tarpaulin 95.11% against the 95 gate with a +0.01% delta). The managed pre-push hook re-ran the same gate on push. The coverage threshold in .ci/coverage-threshold.txt was not touched. GitHub CI runs only on pull_request and pushes to main, so no branch run exists to check; shipment will exercise CI on main.
